result.summary: Makes the default combined fee estimator fall back to the block policy estimate whenever the mempool estimator is unavailable, returning an error only if the block policy estimate also fails. Changes the mempool estimator to return an error rather than the relay fee floor when the mempool is too sparse to calculate block-template percentiles. Also clears the mempool estimator's tracked mined-block history if the mempool fails to load at startup, and renames the combined estimator RPC option and enum from "none" to "auto" (retaining "none" for backward compatibility).
result.problem: When the mempool estimator is not ready (such as during initial startup, before tracking enough blocks, or under low coverage), the default combined estimator failed completely instead of using available block policy data. Furthermore, when the mempool was empty or sparse (such as after a restart without persistence or with a corrupt mempool.dat), the mempool estimator returned the fee floor, causing significant fee underestimation and risking stuck transactions.
evidence: PR description: "Previously, case (ii) with a healthy mempool will returned the fee rate floor (the higher of the minimum relay fee and the current mempool minimum fee). This can be a significant underestimation, since the now-missing mempool may have held much higher-feerate transactions."

Commit 305f7df895: "When the mempool fails to load at startup... init notifies the fee_rate_estimator_man, which clears its tracked mined-block window. Otherwise the estimator would keep a window describing a mempool the node no longer has and, once the mempool refilled, serve an estimate built on it."
result.changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the design; includes minor test additions and rebases since the previous version.
result.card: Makes the default combined fee estimator in estimatesmartfee fall back to the block policy estimate whenever the mempool estimator is unready, instead of failing or returning an error. Changes the mempool estimator to return an error rather than the relay fee floor when the mempool is too sparse to fill block percentiles, preventing severe fee underestimation on nodes with an empty or freshly reset mempool. Additionally, clears the mempool estimator's mined-block history when mempool loading fails at startup to avoid stale estimates, and renames the RPC estimator option from 'none' to 'auto'.

risk.why: A flaw in fee estimation fallback or percentile calculation could cause wallet users or RPC callers to significantly underpay or overpay transaction fees, resulting in delayed confirmations or wasted funds.
